Question: Which model performs best overall on both the CVR and CTCVR tasks?
Evidence:
[E1] (table, Table 2, page 4): Table 2: Comparison of different models on Public Dataset.
Values (cite as cells):
  row 'BASE': 'AUC(mean ± std) on CVR task' = 66.00 ± 0.37; 'AUC(mean ± std) on CTCVR task' = 62.07 ± 0.45
  row 'AMAN': 'AUC(mean ± std) on CVR task' = 65.21 ± 0.59; 'AUC(mean ± std) on CTCVR task' = 63.53 ± 0.57
  row 'OVERSAMPLING': 'AUC(mean ± std) on CVR task' = 67.18 ± 0.32; 'AUC(mean ± std) on CTCVR task' = 63.05 ± 0.48
  row 'UNBIAS': 'AUC(mean ± std) on CVR task' = 66.65 ± 0.28; 'AUC(mean ± std) on CTCVR task' = 63.56 ± 0.70
  row 'DIVISION': 'AUC(mean ± std) on CVR task' = 67.56 ± 0.48; 'AUC(mean ± std) on CTCVR task' = 63.62 ± 0.09
  row 'ESMM-NS': 'AUC(mean ± std) on CVR task' = 68.25 ± 0.44; 'AUC(mean ± std) on CTCVR task' = 64.44 ± 0.62
  row 'ESMM': 'AUC(mean ± std) on CVR task' = 68.56 ± 0.37; 'AUC(mean ± std) on CTCVR task' = 65.32 ± 0.49

claims.text: The 'ESMM' model achieves the highest AUC(mean ± std) on both the CVR and CTCVR tasks.
The 'BASE' model has an AUC(mean ± std) of 66.00 ± 0.37 on the CVR task and 62.07 ± 0.45 on the CTCVR task.
